title: State Entropy Regularization for Robust Reinforcement Learning

predicted_errors.error_location: Theorem 3.1 and Table 1 (worst-case reward for state, policy, and state-action entropy)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The stated worst-case reward for state entropy regularization is 'r(s,a) - α log d_P^π(s) - ε'. Substituting this into the uncertainty set constraint shows it does not saturate the bound; the correct worst-case reward that makes the constraint tight is 'r(s,a) - α log d_P^π(s) - ε - α log S' (an extra -α log S term). Analogously, the policy entropy worst-case reward should include -α log A, and state-action entropy should include -α log(SA). The current values are feasible but not the true adversarial rewards.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.3 (Sensitivity to rollout budget), reference to 'Figure 5(b)'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text says 'Figure 5(b) shows that with very limited rollouts...', but the figure caption assigns (b) to 'Reward Shift' and (c) to 'Rollouts Per Entropy Estimation Ablation'. The rollout ablation is subfigure (c), not (b).

The statement labeled 'Theorem 3.3' is not a formal mathematical theorem; it is a paragraph of qualitative discussion ('an approximate lower bound on worst-case performance under kernel uncertainty can be characterized...'). A precise lower bound or inequality that constitutes a theorem is missing. The appendix proof exists but the main text lacks a proper theorem statement.

The proof claims that for every temperature α the regularized optimal policy will have q ≈ 1/2, arguing 'for every temperature α we can make ε arbitrarily small'. This ignores the dependence of the entropy term on the state distribution and does not rigorously analyze the regularized objective. The existence of an MDP that makes the regularized policy uniform is not adequately justified, leaving a gap in the proof.

Theorem 4.1 assumes 'there exists an uncertainty set function ... satisfying the robust return condition over all MDPs' without defining the robust return condition. The statement is ambiguous and lacks a precise formulation, making it impossible to verify the claimed contradiction.
